startup_idea: Notes and past papers for juniors at my college, sold before exams
mission: Sell exam-week note bundles, made from toppers' notes and past papers, to juniors on one campus.
problem: First- and second-years skip classes, then panic the week before mid-sems with no clean notes for subjects like DBMS and OS.
target_customer: First- and second-year B.Tech students at one campus who study in the last 7 days before an exam and already pay for printouts.

financial_snapshot.burn_breakdown: Scanning and printing: ₹500; Posters at the canteen and hostel: ₹1,000; Instagram story boosts (marketing budget): ₹1,000; Google Drive: ₹0; Notion: ₹0; Razorpay Payment Links: ₹0

go_to_market: Class WhatsApp groups: Post one free sample page in 6 first-year groups the week before mid-sems
Instagram story boosts: Boost one story a week to students within 2 km of campus
Message 20 juniors from your own club or hostel
Give the first 5 buyers a second subject free for a review
Ask each buyer to forward the sample page to one class group
product_mvp: Unit-wise note bundle per subject, with the last 3 years of papers
Pay by UPI through a payment link, get the Drive link on WhatsApp
Ask 3 toppers for their DBMS and OS notes in exchange for ₹20 per bundle sold
Scan and sort the notes by unit
Collect the last 3 years of papers for both subjects
Make one Notion page with subjects and prices
Post one free sample page in 6 first-year WhatsApp groups

competition.name: Free PDFs in class WhatsApp groups
competition.differentiator: Ours are sorted by unit, checked by a topper and match this semester's syllabus.

competition.name: Photocopy shops near campus
competition.differentiator: No queue the night before the exam, and the notes are searchable.

tools.name: Razorpay Payment Links
tools.note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

final_verdict:
Workable for one campus if about 21 juniors buy each month. The price fits an exam-week panic buy, and the costs are low enough to survive a slow first month.

Biggest risk: A buyer posts the bundle in a class group and nobody needs to pay after that.
